definitions.explanation: The juice squeezed from lemons, used in cooking, drinks, and as a seasoning. Can refer to both freshly squeezed juice and bottled lemon juice.

examples.japanese: レモン{汁|じる}をかける。
examples.english: To drizzle lemon juice on something.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}にレモン{汁|じる}を{加|くわ}える。
examples.english: To add lemon juice to the dish.

examples.japanese: りんごの{変色|へんしょく}を{防|ふせ}ぐために、レモン{汁|じる}を{少|すこ}し{垂|た}らすとよい。
examples.english: To prevent apples from discoloring, it helps to add a few drops of lemon juice.

notes:
A straightforward compound of the loanword レモン (lemon) and {汁|じる} (juice, liquid). In recipes, レモン{汁|じる} is one of the most frequently called-for ingredients. The reading じる (not しる) is standard in this compound.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- レモン{汁|じる}をかける: to sprinkle lemon juice
- レモン{汁|じる}を{絞|しぼ}る: to squeeze lemon juice
- レモン{汁|じる}{大|おお}さじ1: one tablespoon of lemon juice
- レモン{汁|じる}を{加|くわ}える: to add lemon juice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- レモン{果汁|かじゅう}: lemon juice — a more formal term, often used on product labels
- {柑橘類|かんきつるい}の{果汁|かじゅう}: citrus juice — the broader category
- {酢|す}: vinegar — sometimes used as a substitute for lemon juice in cooking
